name: Small Business
title: Free Small Business Invoice Template
description: A free small business invoice template with a centered letterhead and a ruled strip of invoice details: number, dates, terms and amount due. Download as PDF.
summary: A centered letterhead and a ruled strip of invoice facts. The small-business standard.
intro: A centered letterhead, then every fact an accounts department looks for, the number, the dates, the terms and the amount due, in one ruled strip.
explanation: Most small businesses invoice other businesses, and their invoices land in an accounts payable queue. The person processing them doesn’t know you; they need the invoice number, the due date and the amount quickly, and in the same place every time.

This template sets your logo and name as a centered letterhead and gathers the invoice facts into a ruled strip beneath it. The table is conventional (description, quantity, unit price, amount), so any bookkeeper recognizes it at a glance.
It suits shops, printers, caterers, wholesalers, studios and service businesses selling to other businesses: anyone who wants an invoice that looks established and gets processed without questions.
fieldsTitle: What to put on a small business invoice

fields.name: Business details
fields.text: Your business name, logo, address and contact line. Add your tax or VAT number where clients need it.

fields.name: Invoice number
fields.text: A unique number in sequence. The [invoice number generator](/tools/invoice-number-generator/) helps you choose a format.

fields.name: Dates and terms
fields.text: The issue date, payment terms and due date, together in the strip.

fields.name: Products or services
fields.text: Each item with quantity and unit price. Use the client’s own product or service names where you can.

fields.name: Discount
fields.text: A percentage or a fixed amount, for repeat orders or early payment, applied before tax.

fields.name: Delivery
fields.text: Shipping or delivery as the separate charge beneath the tax.

fields.name: Payment
fields.text: Every way you accept payment, and what reference to quote.

steps.title: Open the example
steps.text: Customize this invoice opens a print shop’s invoice in the generator.

steps.title: Your letterhead
steps.text: Add your logo and business details once; they carry over to every new invoice.

steps.title: The order
steps.text: Enter the client and each item. Add a discount, tax and delivery if they apply.

steps.title: Download and send
steps.text: Download the PDF and send it to the client’s accounts address. Your next invoice number is suggested automatically.

faqs.q: What makes an invoice look professional?
faqs.a: Consistency and clarity: the same layout every time, your details at the top, a unique number, clear dates and terms, items a client recognizes, correct totals, and how to pay. Typography helps; a busy design doesn’t.
No. A clearly set business name works as a letterhead. If you have a logo, add it once in the generator and it appears on every invoice.

faqs.q: How should a small business number invoices?
faqs.a: In one unique sequence, never reusing a number. A prefix and year (INV-2026-0042) makes them easy to find. See [how to number invoices](/invoice-guides/how-to-number-invoices/).

faqs.q: Can I add my tax registration number?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter it in the Tax ID field and it prints with your business details.
